title: When one B-flat clarinet replaced two
summary: Clarinetists stopped needing both A and B-flat clarinets once they learned to play everything on B-flat.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: Well, let me just jump around. When did they start using just one clarinet? Do you remember?
After the fellas began to learn to play a B clarinet, make everything on a B clarinet, without using the E.
Was that here in New Orleans? Right here. Oh, they were learning while you were standing?

Right here. Charlie McCurdy's always used a B clarinet. You see, he used to use a set of clarinet. He used to use an A and a B. Mm-hmm.
